articles.title: Fantasy Football: What to expect from some of the buzziest names in preseason heading into Week 1
articles.summary: Matt Okada looks at players who gained hype during the preseason and whether or not we should buy it going into Week 1.
articles.body:
After a full month of ADP Risers and Fallers here at Yahoo, it's time to look back at the buzziest names of the preseason to determine who will (and won't) live up to the hype. Between rookie reveals, depth chart shuffling and injuries, the following six names saw the most notable late surges in fantasy football drafts.

Will they be worth it at their closing price? I've got thoughts.

In the Aug. 25 version of the column , I had Dalton Schultz as an Honorable Mention Riser and one of my favorite sleeper tight ends. One week later, he cracked the official list with a 17-spot jump in ADP. Granted, he's still going in the 11th round as the 19th tight end off the board, so he's more of a sneaky dart throw than a significant draft investment. But that also makes him a pretty good bet to return value at his ADP. Most of the other tight ends going in his range — Oronde Gadsden II, Chig Okonkwo, Terrance Ferguson, Hunter Henry — have much more competition for targets and much lower fantasy floors.

On the flip side, Schultz doesn't have much runway for a "top-tier breakout." He did once finish as the TE3 overall ... but that was five years ago in Dallas. Even if he's the No. 2 target in Houston behind Nico Collins, the overall pie is probably not big enough for Schultz's piece to win you a fantasy league. Still, if you pass on tight end all the way through the single-digit rounds and are looking for a high-floor option to start early in the season, Schultz is probably your man.

Where Schultz is safe, simple and sort of a known commodity, Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd is the complete opposite. He saw a massive late surge in ADP due to the Josh Jacobs' legal investigation, which landed the Green Bay starter on the commissioner's exempt list. That has left Lloyd atop the depth chart, along with Chris Brooks and late trade acquisition Kaleb Johnson. All signs point to Lloyd seeing the bulk of the running back touches in Jacobs' absence, so his fantasy value will come down to his efficiency and the length of said absence.

It's tough to predict the production, as Lloyd has only logged seven touches in the two years since he was drafted, but he was a third-round pick out of USC and should be able to put up relatively average numbers in a good offense. Unfortunately, it's even tougher to project how long Jacobs will be gone, pending legal proceedings, Roger Goodell's decision-making process and a potential NFL suspension. Lloyd ended up at an ADP of RB32 in the eighth round, which makes sense if we assume Jacobs misses roughly half the season. If he's back much sooner (unlikely), Lloyd would be a bust at that draft cost. If he misses the entire year, Lloyd would be a steal. Where we currently stand (with very little information), I like taking Lloyd right around that range, but no higher.

Over the last two weeks of August, Mike Washington Jr. was the top ADP riser in two consecutive columns, jumping more than 40 spots in that span alone. It started with his explosive preseason — 186 scrimmage yards on 25 touches in total — but really kicked into gear with Ashton Jeanty's ankle sprain. There was very little clear reporting on Jeanty's injury, so speculation about an early-season absence abounded, and Washington's ADP rocketed up as the clear No. 2 in the backfield. Jeanty is currently on track to play Week 1 after all, so Washington's shot at being an RB1 to start the year is fading.

However, there's speculation that he may have carved out a surprisingly significant role in the offense. Raiders GM John Spytek has said that new HC Klint Kubiak "stood on the table" for Washington and loved him as a scheme fit ... a curious consideration, since Jeanty is an inherited asset from the previous coaching regime. And of course, Kubiak ran an incredibly frustrating two-back committee in Seattle last year, with Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet. In the end, this feels a little more like cold water on Year 2 Jeanty hype than the arrival of Washington as a fantasy star. But as the RB43 in the 11th round, he certainly has a ton of upside as a backup to the incumbent starter.

At this point, Stefon Diggs may have quietly receded from your social media feed, as his ADP rise took place in early August after signing with the Washington Commanders. Still, he ultimately went from a deep sleeper in late July to an eighth-round pick in early September. Was that jump too much? The former free agent turns 33 years old in November and it took months for someone to sign him this offseason (possibly due in part to off-the-field issues). It was only a one-year, $8 million contract with the Commanders, and Terry McLaurin is still present atop the depth chart.

Smoke and mirrors! I love where Diggs ended up in drafts, going around WR42 at the 9-10 turn, between Quentin Johnston and Jordyn Tyson (who's on short-term injured reserve). Diggs was extremely efficient in New England last season, catching an absurd 83.3% of his targets while averaging 11.9 yards per reception. The only players to run 250+ routes and average more yards per route run than Diggs in 2025 (2.4) were Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Zay Flowers and Amon-Ra St. Brown. And while McLaurin is a great downfield option, Diggs might be the better possession receiver for Jayden Daniels and Co. I've projected Diggs to lead the team in catches, and you're not going to find that in the eighth round very often. If you play with any form of PPR scoring, I think Diggs is a draft value, even after climbing several rounds last month.

Throughout our four weeks of ADP Risers and Fallers, Jonathon Brooks was the second-most common name, appearing as the foil to Chuba Hubbard's injury-instigated fall in early August and featuring in the column shortly thereafter. Brooks started outside the top-100 picks and has jumped 20-30 spots since, specifically when referencing Yahoo Plus ADP over the last seven days. Personally, I've been riding the hype train since Rico Dowdle's departure, so you can guess where I fall on this one.

Carolina drafted Brooks early in the second round two years ago — capital that suggests RB1 expectations — and he just has not seen the field thanks to horrible injury misfortune. He's missed practice recently due to "general soreness," but it doesn't seem like a legitimate concern. And while Hubbard's hamstring has recovered and he should play in Week 1, I still believe this will be a Brooks-favored committee early and that the younger back will take a comfortable lead by October (at the latest). He's going just behind Dowdle (now in Pittsburgh) and Lloyd (see above), neither of whom has as clear a path to RB1 touches all season. For relatively low risk, you're getting a shot at a young, high-end fantasy starter with Jonathan Taylor draft capital and a Jamaal Charles skill set (per pre-draft scouting comps). That's a shot you should take nine times out of 10.

Finally, the biggest riser of the late offseason, Mr. Buzz himself, rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling. The 49ers' surprise pick at 33rd overall was the star of the preseason and the talk of training camp, and was the only player to make the top-three risers in the column all four weeks. He went from essentially undrafted (outside the top 150) to the back end of the ninth round, ahead of Diggs (see above) and a number of other tried-and-true veteran starters.

Stribling snagged 11 of 13 targets (on 22 routes) in the preseason, scoring 16.4 half-PPR fantasy points in what was essentially three quarters of play the first two weeks. He also looked very impressive doing it. And amid his meteoric rise, Mike Evans battled multiple soft tissue injuries, Christian Kirk was placed on IR (calf), George Kittle continued rehabbing an Achilles injury, Deebo Samuel Sr. was signed out of desperation and Christian McCaffrey has missed practice time (though allegedly as part of a plan to keep him fresh).

It's not a stretch to say Stribling is San Fran's healthiest pass-catcher, and it may not even be a stretch to say he's their best pass-catcher (in a positional vacuum). Certainly, he has as good a chance as almost anyone in this range of drafts to be his team's WR1 and a fantasy WR2. Once again, I'd snap up this value — even over names like DK Metcalf and Alec Pierce ahead of him — on the prospect that he plays well ahead of his draft price in his rookie season.

articles.title: History made! Lionel Messi, 39, breaks Ronaldo’s Ballon d’Or record and sets new mark with stunning 2026 nomination
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi, at 39, breaks Cristiano Ronaldo's Ballon d'Or nomination record, achieving a historic 20-year span. Discover the details of his career and latest nomination for the prestigious award.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has created another piece of Ballon d'Or history at the age of 39, breaking a record previously held by Cristiano Ronaldo and becoming the first player ever to span 20 years between his first and most recent nomination for the prestigious award.Messi's inclusion on the 2026 Ballon d'Or shortlist, announced by France Football on Tuesday, means his story with the award now stretches from 2006 to 2026. No player before him had managed to remain a Ballon d'Or nominee across such a long period.Messi's Ballon d'Or journey now covers two decadesMessi first appeared among the Ballon d'Or nominees in 2006, when he was still a teenage Barcelona player. He received two votes that year, beginning what has become one of the longest individual runs in the history of the award.Twenty years later, he is still there.His nomination for 2026 takes his career total to 17 Ballon d'Or nominations, according to Spanish newspaper AS, putting him second behind Ronaldo for the overall number of appearances on the shortlist.But Messi now has something his great rival never achieved: the longest span between a player's first and latest Ballon d'Or nominations.Ronaldo previously held that record after appearing on the shortlist from 2004 to 2022, a span of 18 years.Messi's new mark stretches that to 20 years.The all-time list for the longest span between first and most recent Ballon d'Or nominations now has Messi at the top, followed by Ronaldo with 18 years, Luka Modrić with 16, Karim Benzema with 15 and Paolo Maldini with 14.It is a different kind of record from simply accumulating nominations. Ronaldo still leads Messi for the total number of appearances, with 18 nominations to Messi's 17, but Messi has now surpassed him for longevity.And that distinction makes the latest nomination particularly remarkable.Messi is no longer in the phase of his career when a Ballon d'Or nomination would be considered routine. At 39, he is now the oldest player to be nominated in the 21st century, surpassing Ronaldo's previous mark of 37 when he was nominated in 2022.The all-time record remains with Stanley Matthews, who was 41 when he won the inaugural Ballon d'Or in 1956.Also read: Despite a 4-year snub, Ronaldo still holds one major Ballon d'Or record Messi perhaps will never matchFrom teenage nominee to eight-time winnerMessi's first nomination was only the beginning of an extraordinary relationship with the award.He has since gone on to win the Ballon d'Or a record eight times, more than any other player in history.His victories came in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021 and 2023.Ronaldo remains second with five wins, meaning the pair have dominated the award to an extent no other players have matched. They are the only two players to have won the Ballon d'Or more than once this century.Messi's 2026 nomination therefore creates an unusual split between the two rivals.Ronaldo still has more total nominations — 18 to 17 — while Messi now owns the record for the longest period between a player's first and latest nomination.And Messi has managed to set that record despite spending the final stages of his career outside Europe's traditional football powerhouses.He is the only active MLS player included on the 2026 men's shortlist, standing alone among the representatives from Major League Soccer while the rest of the 30-player list is largely made up of stars from Europe's leading competitions and the Saudi Pro League.His nomination comes after another major international campaign with Argentina.Messi helped Argentina reach the 2026 World Cup final, scoring eight goals and providing four assists during the tournament. He also briefly became the all-time leading World Cup scorer with 21 goals, before Kylian Mbappé overtook him. The campaign added another remarkable chapter to an international career that has already included the World Cup and Copa AméricaAlso read: Despite a 4-year snub, Ronaldo still holds one major Ballon d'Or record Messi perhaps will never matchAlso read: Why Cristiano Ronaldo wasn’t nominated for the 2026 Ballon d’OrHe had also announced his international retirement last month, making his continued presence on the Ballon d'Or shortlist even more striking.At club level, Messi also enjoyed a successful domestic campaign with Inter Miami, completing a domestic double before returning to the Ballon d'Or shortlist.That does not necessarily make him the favourite to win the prize this year. Rodri currently leads the contenders, with players such as Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal also among the leading candidates after their respective seasons and the events of the World Cup.But the significance of Messi's nomination goes beyond whether he wins another trophy.A teenager who first appeared on the Ballon d'Or list in 2006 has now been nominated again in 2026, two full decades later.Ronaldo's 18-year span once represented the benchmark for longevity at the very top of the award.Messi has now moved past it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El español Thomas Christiansen renueva como seleccionador de Panamá hasta 2030
articles.standfirst: "¡La historia continúa! Thomas Christiansen sigue al mando de la Selección Mayor Masculina de Panamá por los próximos cuatro años. El 2030 nos espera"
articles.summary: "¡La historia continúa! Thomas Christiansen sigue al mando de la Selección Mayor Masculina de Panamá por los próximos cuatro años. El 2030 nos espera"
articles.body: La Federación Panameña de Fútbol (FPF) anunció la continuidad del entrenador de la selección absoluta, el hispano-danés Thomas Christiansen, hasta 2030. El anuncio se produjo con una publicación en las redes sociales: "¡La historia continúa! Thomas Christiansen sigue al mando de la Selección Mayor Masculina de Panamá por los próximos cuatro años. El 2030 nos espera". Con esta renovación la FPF dejó claro el siguiente paso para el proceso eliminatorio hacia el Mundial de 2030 de la mano del técnico, responsable de que la roja centroamericana jugara en 2026 su segunda Copa del Mundo. Christiansen comparecerá ante los medios de comunicación, en el inicio de un nuevo ciclo como seleccionador de Panamá, para dar a conocer la nueva estructura de las selecciones masculinas de la federación. Desde su llegada al banquillo en 2020, Christiansen dirigió a Panamá en 92 partidos, con un balance de 44 victorias, 21 empates y 27 derrotas. En su gestión, la selección alcanzó en tres ocasiones consecutivas el 'Final Four' de la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf y obtuvo el subcampeonato del torneo, además de disputar la final de la Copa Oro de 2023, la mejor actuación panameña en esa competición desde 2005. El técnico también condujo a Panamá en la Copa América de 2024, en la que avanzaron por primera vez a los cuartos de final. Christiansen promovió la incorporación de nuevos jugadores y consolidó una base que tomó el relevo de los referentes que protagonizaron la clasificación al Mundial de Rusia 2018. En junio de 2025 se convirtió en el entrenador con más partidos dirigidos en la historia de la selección absoluta de Panamá, reflejo de la continuidad de un proyecto respaldado por la federación. Bajo su dirección, Panamá también registró la mejor posición de su historia en la clasificación mundial de la FIFA al ascender desde el puesto ochenta y uno, que ocupaba en septiembre de 2020, hasta el veintinueve en 2025. Tras su participación en el Mundial de 2026, la selección descendió al puesto cuarenta y cuatro del escalafón.

articles.title: EPL demands a different kind of intensity: Alexander Isak
articles.summary: Football News: Alexander Isak believes Liverpool's greatest strength extends beyond tactics or personnel. It lies in the calm authority of captain Virgil van Dijk, I.
articles.body: Alexander Isak believes Liverpool's greatest strength extends beyond tactics or personnel. It lies in the calm authority of captain Virgil van Dijk, Isak told TOI in an interaction facilitated by JioStar. The Swedish striker spoke about adapting to Arne Slot's possession-based system, and now, Andoni Iraola's high-intensity football, returning from injury, and the passion of Liverpool's global fanbase. Excerpts:Liverpool looks like a team in its rebuilding phase. From a striker's perspective, what makes this Liverpool team different from the previous champions?Yes, it's a completely new team with a lot of new players and young players. I don't really know how to explain it. It's just that different players make it a different team.You've now played under Andoni Iraola, who is known for his vertical high-intensity football, as well as Arne Slot, whose approach is more controlled, possession-based. As a striker, what is the biggest adjustment you had to make without the ball?I think for me, it's been about defending in positions where I would be in a good position when we win the ball, ready to attack, ready to counter quickly. So, it's always about thinking where you're at.That spell on the sidelines, did that change the way you watch football? Were you analysing defenders and movements more than when you were actually playing?No, not really. I mean, when I was injured, I didn't watch too much. I followed Liverpool and that was about it. And then I was just doing my rehab.Fans in India stay up late to watch matches. What is your message to them?Of course, we appreciate all support from overseas where we understand that the times are not always very suitable. Hopefully we can do well and have a good season, which makes staying up late more worth it.What has struck you the most about Liverpool as a club?The fans. Their passion and dedication to the club is incredible. Liverpool is a club rich in culture, history, and tradition. It's been really nice to see that up close.You've played in Germany, Spain before you came to England, so how different is the Premier League compared to these other leagues?Every league has its own style and football culture. The Premier League is more physical and faster. Spain is more controlled and technical. There are pros and cons to every league, but the Premier League demands a different kind of intensity.Your captain Virgil van Dijk picked you as the Liverpool player to watch out for this season, so what are your reactions? And what qualities about Van Dijk do you admire the most?I was surprised to hear that. There are so many players in this squad who can have a big season. Hopefully all of us can step up. As for Van Dijk, the thing that stands out most is how calm he is. Whether he's on the ball or defending, he never looks rushed. That calmness spreads through the whole team.(Watch Liverpool vs Fulham in the Premier League 2026-27 on Sept 12, 7:30 PM onwards, LIVE & Exclusive on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Marc Bartra y el penalti del Madrid: "Es grave que se manipulen imágenes para presionar a los árbitros"
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid reclamó una posible invasión del área de Marc Bartra y la repetición del penalti que Mbappé falló en el Betis 1-0 Madrid
articles.summary: El Real Madrid reclamó una posible invasión del área de Marc Bartra y la repetición del penalti que Mbappé falló en el Betis 1-0 Madrid
articles.body: Marc Bartra, 'Pichichi' de la Champions League tras marcar dos goles en el triunfo del Real Betis por 2-3 ante el Lille, ha opinado sobre el polémico penalti del Betis 1-0 Real Madrid. Álvaro Valles le detuvo un penalti a Kylian Mbappé y posterior intervino Marc Bartra para despejar el rechace. El Real Madrid reclamó una posible invasión del área del central bético y, por tanto, la repetición del lanzamiento. "¿El penalti en La Cartuja? Quiero pensar que el VAR no sabía el reglamento", declaró Mourinho en rueda de prensa. "Es bastante grave que se manipulen imágenes para presionar a los árbitros", dijo el defensa catalán, ex del F.C. Barcelona, en declaraciones que reproduce Teledeporte. Marc Bartra destacó que "lo bueno es que hay muchas cámaras y si el CTA ha sacado una imagen... Yo estaba completamente seguro de que no había pisado, calculé los tiempos perfecto, puse el pie en el límite". "Yo lo estaba viendo en casa, pero lo veía con tranquilidad, porque si sacan la que es sé que no estoy pisando, lo tengo clarísimo. Lo tenía en mente, lo tenía trabajado. Sabía que por mí no era", subrayó. EL CTA (Comité Técnico de Árbitros) concluyó que el penalti no debió repetirse y que la posición de Bartra era legal.

articles.title: El Liverpool de los hinchas
articles.standfirst: Pese a los millonarios fichajes del club, Alisson y Van Dijk siguen siendo los más queridos por la afición. Los autores de sus murales explican a MARCA por qué habitan ya junto a los mitos
articles.summary: Pese a los millonarios fichajes del club, Alisson y Van Dijk siguen siendo los más queridos por la afición. Los autores de sus murales explican a MARCA por qué habitan ya junto a los mitos
articles.body: Barcolá por 125 millones, Jacquet por 63,6 o Víctor Muñoz por 40 llegaron este verano al Liverpool como en el anterior hicieron Isak por 145, Wirtz por 125 o Ekitiké por 95. Sin embargo, lo que no se compra es el cariño de la grada. Los grandes desembolsos no confunden a la hinchada red. Lo demuestra con sus actos y se plasma en los numerosos murales que brotan en los alrededores de Anfield honrando a los más grandes de la historia del club. La condición de mito no se regala, se gana. Como han hecho las dos únicas leyendas vivas, el portero Alisson y el capitán Van Dijk. Lo confiesan en MARCA Mark Murwalls y John Culshaw, los artistas callejeros encargados de perpetuar su memoria. "Virgil es una figura enorme para el Liverpool y sus aficionados. Llegó en un momento en el que no se había conseguido ningún éxito durante muchísimos años y su llegada formó parte de esa reconstrucción junto con jugadores como Alisson. Reforzaron esa defensa y convirtieron al equipo en un conjunto formidable y de talla mundial que posteriormente ganó todos los trofeos que conocemos, incluida la Premier. Por eso consideramos muy importante que Virgil tuviera su homenaje aunque históricamente los murales se han encargado de representar a leyendas del pasado. Decidimos que queríamos pintar a uno de los jugadores más contemporáneos para añadirlo a figuras como Firmino, a quien ya habíamos representado, pero nunca habíamos pintado murales de jugadores que siguieran en activo", justifica Mark sobre la excepción que supuso Van Dijk. “Después de que Luis Díaz fuera elegido como el fichaje de la temporada, quise hacer una votación popular sobre qué jugador quería ver la afición representado, así que la sometí a votación y fue abrumadora. ¡Alisson obtuvo alrededor del 90% de los votos!”, explica John sobre lo que le llevó a inmortalizar al portero una vez que encontró la pared adecuada cerca de estadio tras pedir permiso a sus propietarios, la casa de apuestas William Hill. "Sentí un poco más de presión al pintarlo al ser una elección de los aficionados, aunque, para ser sincero, si yo hubiera votado también habría elegido a Alisson, es el mejor portero del mundo y tenemos suerte de tenerlo", cuenta. En el caso de Van Dijk, el gigante que vacunó al Atlético en el último minuto el año pasado, su mural supuso una doble satisfacción para su autor. "Existía la incertidumbre de que su contrato llegara a su fin y queríamos asegurarnos de que tuviera ese homenaje. Pero para cuando acabé el mural, su contrato se había resuelto. Así que sentimos que el mural era, en realidad, más una celebración no sólo de todo lo que ha conseguido en el Liverpool, sino también del hecho de que se comprometía a dedicarle al club los próximos años, lo cual fue fantástico para todos los aficionados", confiesa Murwalls. De ahí el lema impresionado en la pared: 'Su historia... fue siempre el Liverpool'. A Culshaw, por su parte, el mayor quebradero de cabeza al que se enfrentó fue su propósito de sobre impresionar la acción con la que Alisson entró en la historia del Liverpool como el único portero en marcar en partido oficial: un testarazo en el 95' frente al West Bromwich que valía una clasificación para la Champions. "Las imágenes en línea de ese cabezazo no eran lo suficientemente buenas, así que me di cuenta de que tendría que ser algo más gráfico. Yo mismo lo intenté, pero no eran lo que quería y sabía que Cally, un artista digital afincado en Liverpool, ya había pintado uno, así que me puse en contacto con él y le pregunté si me dejaba usar una de sus imágenes existentes para pintarla. Obviamente, aunque el retrato tiene muchos detalles y me llevó seis horas, el dibujo gráfico me llevó más tiempo, todo el día, porque trabajaba subido a una escalera y me subía y me bajaba constantemente para asegurarme de que todo estuviera en su sitio”, recuerda. Aunque para realismo, la inauguración del mural de Van Dijk. "Queríamos asegurarnos de que estuviera al tanto, que lo aprobara y que también aportara cualquier sugerencia. Pero fue un honor absoluto que viniera a firmar el mural. Fue un día muy especial. Intentamos mantenerlo en secreto, peo fue imposible, había cientos de personas en las calles y a pesar de ello Virgil, que estaba abrumado por el mural y el apoyo recibido, se aseguró de darles a todas y cada una de ellas la oportunidad de saludarlo, tomar una foto o conseguir su autógrafo. Fue absolutamente increíble, las fotos y los videos me traen de vuelta muchos recuerdos hermosos de ese día", reconoce. Un reconocimiento que no está reñido con el respeto a los mitos anteriores. Por eso el mural de Alisson, erigido desde el pasado viernes en el cuarto red con más porterías a cero (superó las 137 de Elisha Soctt, se acerca a las 177 de Reina y ve más lejos las 267 de Grobbelaar y las 323 de Ray Clemence), reza 'el mejor portero del mundo', aunque su autor aclare de viva voz que se trata del segundo de la historia del Liverpool en alusión al que se situó bajo palos durante las tres Copas de Europa conquistadas en los 70. "Siempre estamos planeando nuevos murales, pero siento que, por el momento, los murales probablemente serán más legendarios. Mientras el jugador sigue en activo pueden pasar muchas cosas. Sin embargo, sabíamos que Virgil ya había hecho lo suficiente en su carrera como para merecer el suyo, pero en la plantilla actual, aunque cuenta con algunos jugadores emocionantes, en mi opinión tienen que hacer bastante más para ganarse su mural", secunda Mark.

articles.title: El termómetro de Julián
articles.standfirst: Tras firmar 17 goles en 25 apariciones como rojiblanco en la Champions, su competición fetiche mide su estado de recuperación
articles.summary: Tras firmar 17 goles en 25 apariciones como rojiblanco en la Champions, su competición fetiche mide su estado de recuperación
articles.body: Si hay una competición que sirva para calibrar el 'estado de salud' de Julián Alvarez, esa no es otra que la Champions. No ya porque ya la haya levantado actuando como recambio de Haaland en el Manchester City anotando ocho goles en 17 partidos, sino porque esa media de 0,47 dianas por aparición se ha visto casi duplicada desde que juega en el Atlético. Tanto, que sólo Griezmann ha visto puerta más veces con la elástica rojiblanca en la máxima competición continental. Ya fuera en su primera temporada truncada con el doble penalti o en la pasada en la que atravesó tres meses de sequía, la Champions siempre ha mostrado al mejor Julián, manifestándose como su competición fetiche. No en vano, tras marcar siete y diez goles respectivamente, arroja unas cifras de 17 muescas en 25 citas. Un porcentaje del 0,68 que supera ampliamente a Anoine. En este sentido, el máximo goleador de la historia del club anotó 40 dianas en 99 encuentros, promediando 0,4 por duelo. Una muestra de que el inicio de Julián lleva un ritmo que son palabras mayores. De hecho, la Araña, autor del último gol europeo del Atlético (en la ida de las semifinales frente al Arsenal), no ha encadenado más de dos partidos sin ver puerta. Así que, por más que Anfield no le ha resultado propicio durante su experiencia en la Premier, un tanto al Liverpool no sólo mantendría su idilio con la competición, sino que anunciaría que ya está de vuelta.

articles.title: 'Kang-in Lee, ¡acción!'
articles.standfirst: Debuta en Anfield tras jugar ante el Liverpool el último partido de las dos Champions que colecciona. A los 7 años ya rodó un anuncio en Manchester tras ser descubierto en un talent show coreano
articles.summary: Debuta en Anfield tras jugar ante el Liverpool el último partido de las dos Champions que colecciona. A los 7 años ya rodó un anuncio en Manchester tras ser descubierto en un talent show coreano
articles.body: Aunque hoy, en su estreno en la Champions como heredero de Griezmann, será la primera vez que le apunten los focos en Anfield, Kang-in Lee no sólo sabe lo que es dejar en el camino al Liverpool, sino que se presentará como el futbolista más laureado en la Champions de cuantos salten al verde. Una fama y una responsabilidad con la que convive con naturalidad desde los seis años, cuando se erigió en una estrella mediática en Corea del Sur y se gestó su primera visita a Inglaterra. No le hizo falta participar en el 0-2 del pasado 14 de abril en el que el PSG selló el pase a las semifinales de la Champions (lo vivió desde el banquillo) para demostrar su clase al Liverpool. Lo había hecho en el Parque de los Príncipes en la ida, donde aprovechó el tramo final para firmar un 100% de acierto en el pase tras sustituir en el 78' a Doue. Un buen sabor de boca en aquel 2-0 que encauzaba la eliminatoria que, sin saberlo, sería su último servicio en sus dos Orejonas conquistadas consecutivamente con el club galo. Ahora, dispuesto a asumir de rojiblanco mucho mayor protagonismo, Kang-in arranca una nueva era con todo Corea del Sur y buena parte del Oriente asiático pendiente de cada una de sus acciones. Una expectación, en todo caso, que le resulta más que familiar, pues apenas iniciado el colegio ya tenía a todo su país detrás. Fue a raíz de su primera aparición en televisión, en la tercera edición de un 'talent show' infantil llamado Fly Shoot Dori que con su presencia dispararía su difusión. No era para menos, pues lo que era capaz de hacer aquel niño de seis años que lucía el 11 cautivaría tanto al histórico capitán de la selección en el Mundial de 20202, Yoo Sang-Cheol, como al resto de leyendas que ejercían de entrenadores. Su facilidad para el regate, su inteligencia táctica y un disparo impropio para su edad llamaría la atención como nadie más había hecho. De ahí que, al margen de convertirse en una celebridad y ser encasillado con la condición de niño prodigio, Kang-in Lee también se ganaría como premio un viaje a Manchester para rodar un anuncio junto a Park Ji-Sung, por entonces futbolista del United y máximo ídolo del fútbol asiático. Así que, con sólo siete años, y a apenas 50 kilómetros del escenario del partido de esta noche, Kang in rodaba un sketch publicitario para la empresa energética KT en el que se recreaba un icónico gol de Park a Portugal en el Mundial de 2022. Un control con el pecho, un sombrero a un defensa y una volea cruzada con la zurda antes de abrazarse en la banda con su ídolo (Park hacía las veces del seleccionador Guus Hiddink) que pondría de manifiesto que aquel no era un niño cualquiera. Fue sólo el principio de una historia aún por escribir en rojiblanco con jugadas de ese calado. 'Silencio Anfield, el 7 entra a cámara. ¡Accion!'

articles.title: El Arsenal se pone a prueba en Nápoles
articles.standfirst: El campeón inglés y líder actual de la Premier visita el Stadio Maradona
articles.summary: El campeón inglés y líder actual de la Premier visita el Stadio Maradona
articles.body: El vigente subcampeón de Europa y monarca de la Premier League viaja al sur de Italia en un estado de forma inmejorable. Los de Arteta, de nuevo candidatos a llegar muy lejos en la competición continental, se proclamaron campeones de la Community Shield ante el City (goleando, 3-0) y han ganado los primeros tres partidos de la liga inglesa. Vienen, además, de remontar al Chelsea de Xabi Alonso en el derbi de Londres (2-1) y únicamente han encajado un gol, el de los blues, en este inicio de curso. Arteta no tiene quejas, ni bajas (únicamente Saliba), todo lo contrario que su homónimo en el banquillo napolitano: Max Allegri. El de Livorno apenas suma tres puntos de nueve posibles (derrotas ante Como e Inter, dos equipos Champions) en su estreno en el banquillo 'azzurro' y las críticas ya asoman por el estilo de juego que está implantando en 'su' Nápoles. Además, él si tiene bajas... e importantes. Ni McTominay ni Zambo Anguissa estarán hoy ante el Arsenal. O lo que es lo mismo, dos piezas fundamentales del centro del campo napolitano. Arteta y la directiva tenían que inventarse un nuevo Arsenal para mantenerse en la cima. Y tras un verano con movimientos interesantes en el mercado, parece que lo han hecho. La columna vertebral se mantiene pero han entrado piezas en la rotación que añaden versatilidad y fondo de armario al plan 'Gunner'. Repetir lo del pasado curso (final de Champions y título de Premier) no iba a ser fácil. Más de 200 millones ha invertido el equipo londinense en mejorar la plantilla este mercado estival. Nombres como Bruno Guimaraes (pagaron 87,5 millones al Newcastle) o Tzolis (llegó por 40 desde el Brujas) han entrado de lleno al once. Konsa, mientras, también está sumando minutos ante la lesión de Saliba en el centro de la defensa. De momento, se está viendo un Arsenal igual de dominador, con recursos a balón parado (decisivo para los éxitos del pasado curso) pero con más recursos para generar ocasiones. El retorno de Saka (al 100% ya) también ha sido determinante.

articles.title: El eclipse continental del Valencia: 2.374 días sin jugar en Europa
articles.standfirst: Supera su peor racha sin aparecer en competiciones continentales entre 1983 y 1989, una sequía iniciada tras la eliminación ante la Atalanta en marzo de 2020
articles.summary: El club supera este miércoles los 2.373 días que encadenó sin jugar competiciones continentales entre 1983 y 1989, una sequía iniciada tras la eliminación ante la Atalanta en marzo de 2020
articles.body: El Valencia alcanzará este miércoles una cifra que hace apenas unos años parecía inimaginable en Mestalla. El club cumplirá 2.374 días sin disputar un partido de competición europea y establecerá así la peor racha de ausencia continental de sus 107 años de historia. La efeméride, que coincide con el equipo colista de Primera división, arrastra una carga simbólica especial porque supera el anterior registro negativo, fijado entre 1983 y 1989. Aquel periodo, marcado por el descenso a Segunda división y la posterior reconstrucción del equipo, se prolongó durante 2.373 días. Desde este miércoles, el ciclo actual quedará oficialmente como el más largo que ha atravesado el Valencia lejos de los torneos europeos. La travesía del desierto, en expresión del exentrenador blanquinegro Rubén Baraja, comenzó el 10 de marzo de 2020. Aquella noche, en plena irrupción de la pandemia del Covid, el conjunto entonces dirigido por Albert Celades cayó eliminado en los octavos de final de la Liga de Campeones tras perder 3-4 ante la Atalanta en Mestalla a puerta cerrada. Nadie imaginaba entonces que aquella, con la grada vacía, sería la última cita europea del club durante más de seis años y medio como mínimo. Porque el récord todavía está lejos de detenerse. El Valencia ya tiene asegurada una séptima temporada consecutiva fuera de las competiciones continentales y, en el mejor de los escenarios, no podría regresar a Europa hasta el verano de 2027. Eso situaría la ausencia cerca de los 2.700 días. De hecho, este es el objetivo que se marcó el club con el horizonte de la mudanza al Nou Mestalla el verano próximo. Antes de la llegada de Peter Lim en 2014, el Valencia se había clasificado para competiciones europeas en 16 de las 17 temporadas anteriores. Desde entonces, solo lo consiguió en tres campañas y acumula ya nueve cursos sin presencia continental en los doce años del magnate singapurense al frente de la entidad. Durante este tiempo, el equipo ha pasado de pelear por la Liga de Campeones a convivir con objetivos mucho más modestos. En varias temporadas la preocupación principal ha sido evitar el descenso, una realidad impensable para una entidad que durante décadas formó parte del segundo escalón del fútbol europeo. La clasificación actual refleja además que la recuperación continúa lejos. Tras las cuatro primeras jornadas del campeonato, el conjunto dirigido por Carlos Corberán ocupa la última posición de la tabla con un solo punto de doce posibles, una situación que vuelve a alejar cualquier debate sobre aspiraciones europeas. La paradoja es que no hay muchos clubes con el historial europeo del Valencia. El conjunto blanquinegro figura entre las entidades que han levantado al menos siete títulos continentales: dos Copas de Ferias, una Recopa de Europa, una Copa de la UEFA, dos Supercopas de Europa y una Copa Intertoto. A ello se suman las dos finales de la Liga de Campeones disputadas a comienzos de siglo, una etapa que representó el punto más alto de la historia moderna del club. Sin embargo, siete temporadas consecutivas fuera de Europa han tenido también consecuencias en términos de prestigio y visibilidad. El Valencia ha desaparecido del ranking UEFA, una clasificación en la que durante años ocupó posiciones destacadas gracias a su regularidad internacional.

articles.title: La teoría de Álvaro Benito sobre los pitos del Bernabéu a sus jugadores: "Vienen por una herencia"
articles.standfirst: "La gente quiere ver otra cosa. A la gente no le basta con ganar estos partidos por la pegada"
articles.summary: "La gente quiere ver otra cosa. A la gente no le basta con ganar estos partidos por la pegada"
articles.body: Álvaro Benito, futbolista del Real Madrid de 1995 a 2002 que se vio obligado a retirarse del fútbol en 2003 por culpa de las lesiones, se mostró crítico en el programa 'El Larguero' con el juego del equipo de Mourinho en su triunfo por 2-1 contra el Inter de Milán en Champions League. El exfutbolista también realizó su particular diagnóstico sobre los pitos del Santiago Bernabéu a Vinicius y Mbappé cuando ganaban 2-0. "Bueno, los pitos no son de hoy. Esto es una herencia de los dos últimos años, y en el equipo está darle vuelta a la situación", le comentó a Manu Carreño en la Cadena SER. Álvaro Benito subrayó que "yo pienso que los pitos no son por hoy. Hoy el equipo se ha hecho un partido como lo ha hecho, pero yo creo que la gente lo ha dado todo en el campo... Hoy no se puede reprochar actitud al Real Madrid. Falta más pie en el medio, falta más organización... Sin duda, eso todo lo podemos compartir. Pero al equipo no le falta entrega ante el Inter, ni mucho menos". Álvaro Benito sostiene que "yo creo que los pitos vienen por una herencia de estos dos últimos años, donde la gente quiere ver otra cosa. A la gente no le basta con ganar estos partidos por la pegada. La gente quiere ver cambios. Quiere ver cambios en el juego, quiere ver que el equipo no conceda tanto, que controle más los partidos, que sea más regular". "Fíjate en los momentos que ha presionado, ha provocado errores. Muy groseros del Inter, pero hay que estar ahí. Hay que provocarlos porque tú presionas. Si el Real Madrid eso lo hace de forma continuada, va a provocar muchos más errores, va a tener muchas más situaciones. Pero, claro, eso no le da continuidad en el tiempo, en los partidos. Entonces, los rivales, como son los de hoy, que son buenos, pues te salen muchas veces de la presión, tienen muchísimo más el balón que tú, te obligan a defender muchísimos minutos cerca de Courtois. Y con lo que eso conlleva, pues que al final ha habido muchas situaciones con cierto peligro del Inter, claro que sí", compartió. En la rueda de prensa posterior al partido Jose Mourinho habló sobre los pitos del público del Santiago Bernabéu a Vinicius y Mbappé durante el triunfo del Real Madrid ante el Inter en Champions. "No critico a la afición, hablo como entrenador y de mi relación con Vinicus. Merece todo mi respeto. No está a tope, lo vemos todos, pero él lo sabe. Está trabajando mucho para ser este Vinicius que decide partidos. Está trabajando más que nunca. Las pocas veces que no ha podido defender era por fatiga. No es fácil, pero ha tenido una entrega muy buena. Tengo muchísimo respeto por este Vinicius. Ya llegará el momento donde decide partidos", compartió el luso. Respecto a los pitos a Mbappé declaró que "no comento reacciones del público. No lo hago hoy y no lo haré hasta el último momento en el que esté aquí. Cuando se ha ido, le he dado un beso y para mí eso significa respeto para el trabajo con el equipo". "Las opiniones de aficionados son importantes, pero no le puedo decir nada", apuntó.

articles.title: El Betis no olvida y trolea a Mbappé con la expulsión de su hermano Ethan
articles.standfirst: "Cada vez que un Mbappé escucha Real Betis Balompié"
articles.summary: "Cada vez que un Mbappé escucha Real Betis Balompié"
articles.body: El Real Betis ha recurrido a su cuenta de X (Twitter) para trolear Kylian Mbappé con la expulsión de su hermano Ethan. Ethan Mbappé (19 años) fue expulsado en el partido de Champions League que el Betis ganó 2-3 al Lille. En el minuto 56 cuando el árbitro Georgi Kabakov fue al VAR para revisar una acción. Era una agresión de Ethan Mbappé a Natan que le costó al hermano pequeño de Kylian la roja directa. "Cada vez que un Mbappé escucha las palabras 'Real Betis Balompié', publicó el Betis compartiendo una imagen del actor Willem Dafoe. Con este 'troleo' digital el Betis recordaba el triunfo del Betis por 1-0 ante el Madrid, en el que Kylian Mbappé falló un penalti que paró Vallés. El Real Madrid reclamó una posible invasión del área del central bético y, por tanto, la repetición del lanzamiento. "Es bastante grave que se manipulen imágenes para presionar a los árbitros", denunció Marc Bartra recordando la polémica tras el triunfo ante el Lille.

articles.title: Real Madrid, PSG, Liverpool: Ranking Europe's greatest dynasties
articles.summary: Paris St-Germain are eyeing a third successive Champions League crown, but where do they rank against Europe's most dominant clubs?
articles.body:
Some find success sweet but fleeting, others spend years building to the pinnacle, and then there are those whose lasting glory evolves into a dynasty.

Paris St-Germain begin their Champions League campaign on Wednesday hoping to enter that bracket, attempting to become continental champions for a third successive season.

To mark this, we're looking at how the Parisians compare to those clubs who have enjoyed the most dominant eras in European competition.

Some will point out that football existed before the European Champion Clubs' Cup began in 1955 - so apologies to Stan Cullis' 'world-champion' Wolves outfit and the Mitropa Cup's early Vienna heavyweights.

However, this top 10 debate is centred around winning European football's grandest prize.

OK, straight in with the current champions, because this is a dynasty in the making.

PSG have had a lacklustre start to the season - they always do this, don't they? However, you wouldn't bet against Luis Enrique's slick side adding a third successive European crown come next summer.

The Parisians have been France's most dominant force since the arrival of Qatar Sports Investments 15 years ago, but it took a change of approach for the holy grail of continental success to arrive.

"It's the end of the glitter," professed president Nasser Al-Khelaifi after years of lavish spending, ushering out the "flashy, bling-bling" era.

Instead, Enrique arrived in 2023 intent on building a coherent team. There was still significant investment, but on younger players who could be moulded by his philosophy and discipline while given room to flourish.

The result was two scintillating Champions League triumphs.

Talking of discipline. Helenio Herrera, the Argentine-born defender reared in Casablanca and Paris, had already traversed the dugouts of Atletico Madrid, Malaga, Deportivo and Barcelona before landing in Milan in 1960.

Herrera set about implementing his tactical brand of catenaccio at San Siro - one he insisted is misremembered as being more defensive than it actually was - and developing a ruthless counter-attacking team known as 'Grande Inter'.

Winning the Scudetto in 1962-63, Herrera's outfit became the first to lift the European Cup without losing a game the following season as Sandro Mazzola netted twice against Real Madrid in the final.

The Italians defended their crown the following year, despite losing their semi-final first leg at Anfield, edging Benfica in the final. It was the Portuguese giants' second final defeat in three seasons. Some may say they were cursed...

The story goes that Bela Guttmann, fresh from winning the title with Porto, rocked up at Benfica, sacked all the senior players and promoted a talented bunch of youth team players instead.

Those promising youngsters won the title and then went all the way in the European Cup, beating Barcelona in the 1961 final.

That summer, a teenage Eusebio also joined Guttmann's squad and steered them to European glory once more, seeing off Tottenham Hotspur in the semi-final before beating the great Real Madrid in the competition's showpiece.

The legendary Ferenc Puskas scored a first-half hat-trick for the Spaniards, but Eusebio netted twice after the interval to seal Benfica a second successive crown.

Guttmann, buoyed by his remarkable success, left the club after not being offered the pay rise he felt he deserved and the curse the Hungarian boss supposedly put on the club - that they would not win another European trophy for 100 years - has become fable.

Whether the often-disputed story is true or not, the Lisbon giants have not landed another since - losing eight European finals, including three in the 1960s.

This was Bayern's coming of age. Emerging from what was a fiercely competitive West German football scene, the Bavarians - promoted to the Bundesliga less than a decade earlier - were able to establish themselves as heavyweights in Europe.

With a backbone of goalkeeper Sepp Maier, marauding sweeper Franz Beckenbauer and the prolific Gerd Muller, and fresh off West Germany winning the 1974 World Cup, Bayern clinched three on the bounce, despite their domestic form dipping.

In fact, Beckenbauer said Bayern were past their peak after the first European Cup win over Atletico Madrid, but experience carried them through big games.

They beat Leeds in a controversial final in Paris, and then saw off Saint-Etienne the following year.

The teams above make the list for their trophy-winning spells. Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were European champions twice in three years - losing to Jose Mourinho's treble-winning Inter in between - but their dynasty was built on more than silverware.

Guardiola only spent four seasons at Barcelona, but it was an era-defining tenure, the Catalan giants pioneering a brand of football that would be celebrated and copied the world over.

Perhaps the real success of a team is in its legacy. Guardiola's tiki-taka Barcelona built around La Masia graduates Xavi, Andres Iniesta, Sergio Busquets and, of course, Lionel Messi still resonates more than a decade since he left.

Where does this particular Milan dynasty start and end? It was fuelled, of course, by Silvio Berlusconi, who saved the club from bankruptcy in 1986 and appointed the up-and-coming Arrigo Sacchi as boss.

You could argue it continued until a Champions League final defeat by a young Ajax side in 1995. In between, the Rossoneri won back-to-back European Cups in 1989 and '90, then thrashed Cruyff's Barcelona 'Dream Team' in 1994 after defeat in the final the previous season.

In fact, the only campaigns in which Milan did not reach the final were after their quarter-final second leg was abandoned because of floodlight failure while trailing Marseille in 1991. The Serie A giants' refusal to re-enter the pitch for the final minutes of that one also led to them being banned the following year.

From Sacchi to Fabio Capello, through the brilliant Dutch trio of Ruud Gullit, Marco van Basten and Frank Rijkaard to homegrown stars Franco Baresi, Paolo Maldini and Alessandro Costacurta - the Italian core remaining from that 1989 triumph to the defeat by Ajax six years later - Milan were a phenomenal force.

In an era of English dominance on the continent, winning seven of eight European Cups between 1977 and 1984, Liverpool's 'Boot Room' boys led the way.

The Reds won four of those, Nottingham Forest - who could argue they also deserve a spot on the list - went back-to-back and Aston Villa completed the haul.

Liverpool's European pedigree really began when Bill Shankly's side won the Uefa Cup in 1973, the Reds doing it again three years later under Shankly's former assistant Bob Paisley.

Paisley was able to deliver the biggest prize of all the following season in Rome and, after Kenny Dalglish was brought in to replace Hamburg-bound Kevin Keegan, retained the European Cup at Wembley against Club Brugge in 1978 - the Scottish forward netting the winner.

Three years later, after Brian Clough took Forest to the top, Liverpool were European champions again when Alan Kennedy's goal downed Real Madrid in Paris.

Perhaps most impressive is how the Anfield outfit were able to maintain that success through a series of managers. The line of succession from Shankly to Paisley then landed on Joe Fagan, who was in charge when they beat Roma - in Rome - in '84. That was before the Heysel disaste r, and defeat by Juventus, the following year.

Atletico fans look away now. Two finals in three years and twice Diego Simeone's side ran into their Madrid rivals, losing in agonising fashion in both 2014 and 2016.

The second of those also sparked a three-year winning run for the most successful club in European Cup history.

Real Madrid's formula was seemingly simple: construct a team of the world's best players - spearheaded by Cristiano Ronaldo - and stick a legendary former star in charge.

Zinedine Zidane's new-era galacticos just felt inevitable - they always found a way to win, becoming the first club in the Champions League era not only to retain the trophy but to lift three in a row.

After downing Atletico in the first of the three-peat, they beat Juventus and then Liverpool - the latter remembered for Gareth Bale's cameo, Loris Karius' blunders and Sergio Ramos leaving his mark on Mo Salah.

Similar to Guardiola's Barcelona, the influence of this Ajax side was seen far beyond the trophy cabinet. The lineage of their philosophy - via Johan Cruyff - survives through several of the clubs on this list, from Catalonia to Paris.

Rinus Michels was the pioneer, taking Ajax from the threat of relegation to the most dominant side in Europe, losing the 1969 final to AC Milan but returning to win it for the first time two years later with their swaggering brand of Total Football.

Michels left for Barcelona on the back of that success, though Stefan Kovacs was able to retain the trophy the following year and then add a third successive European crown to Ajax's pile with an impressive run that included knocking out Bayern Munich, Real Madrid and then Juventus in the final.

Cruyff, about to win the second of his three Ballon d'Ors, followed Michels to Barcelona and Ajax's dynasty began to fall apart. The legacy, however, remains.

When it comes to dominance, no one compares to the Real Madrid side who stormed to five successive European Cup triumphs after the competition began in 1955.

With the tournament in its infancy, it was perhaps not considered as imperative by certain nations compared to how Champions League participation dominates clubs' thoughts today, but Real Madrid's style and success helped to alter perceptions.

Alfredo Di Stefano, already a world star by the time Real beat Reims in the inaugural final, was an integral part of the Spanish giants' success, the legendary Paco Gento likewise a stalwart (he also won a sixth European Cup in 1966).

Then, in 1958, Madrid added Hungarian genius Ferenc Puskas following his two-year ban for refusing to return to Budapest after the revolution in 1956.

Puskas was 31 when he joined, but scored 35 goals in 39 European Cup games for Real Madrid, including four in the 7-3 win over Frankfurt at Hampden in the 1960 final. Di Stefano grabbed the other three as Madrid made it five on the spin.

articles.title: Gabriel Jesus y su fichaje por el Barça: "Obviamente, dije que sí enseguida"
articles.standfirst: El delantero brasileño explicó cómo vivió la última semana de mercado y cómo surgió la posibilidad de fichar por el conjunto azulgrana
articles.summary: El delantero brasileño explicó cómo vivió la última semana de mercado y cómo surgió la posibilidad de fichar por el conjunto azulgrana
articles.body: Gabriel Jesus llegó al Barcelona casi sobre la bocina. Sólo unos pocos días antes del cierre de mercado el brasileño se convirtió, casi de un día para otro, en el nuevo delantero del conjunto azulgrana. Ahora repasa cómo surgió todo. El ariete explicó al canal SportyTV cómo vivió la situación en verano: "La verdad es que yo estaba entrenándome. Hice toda la pretemporada con el Arsenal, con normalidad. Sabía que no iba a jugar allí o que no iba a tener muchas oportunidades, pero nadie me había dicho nada. Soy un profesional y seguía entrenándome con el grupo". Sin embargo, el jugador no entraba en los planes de Arteta y empezó a trabajar en solitario. "De repente, me pusieron a entrenar por mi cuenta. Seguía entrenándome y dando el máximo para estar preparado por si tenía la oportunidad de volver a jugar al más alto nivel", comentó el jugador, cuyo nombre empezaba a sonar con fuerza para equipos como Everton o Nápoles. Pero todo pegó un enorme giro de guion cuando surgió la opción Barça: "En la última semana todo fue muy rápido. El trabajo de Deco con el presidente, el club y mi representante fue increíble. De un día para otro, tuvimos claro que tenía la oportunidad de venir". Ni se lo pensó. Aceptó la oferta, casi con los ojos cerrados: "Obviamente, dije que sí al Barça enseguida. Estoy muy feliz de estar aquí". El brasileño debutó en Liga ante el Valencia, con algunas ocasiones de gol en los pocos minutos que disputó, y se espera que debute también en Champions este miércoles ante el Feyenoord, equipo con el que estrenó como goleador en Europa cuando militaba en el Manchester City.

articles.title: 2004-05 deja-vu - Can Moyes inspire another fine finish?
articles.summary: Deadline day may have left Everton fans feeling disillusioned, but the side is four games into the season and remains unbeaten, nine goals scored, including...
articles.body:
Deadline day may have left Everton fans feeling disillusioned, but the side is four games into the season and remains unbeaten, nine goals scored, including two in added time to secure a point.

After what was a chaotic close to the transfer window, even by the Toffees' own standards, the performance against Manchester United ironically saw the summer signings playing a key role in the fight.

Jack Grealish and Hayden Hackney came on from the bench to turn the game on its head, Tyrique George scored to equalise before the visitors went back in front, and it was Ainsley Maitland-Niles with a stunning strike to secure the draw in the final few seconds.

The four players showed the resilience needed at Everton now, but there is a sense of deja vu that could give some hope.

David Moyes' highest ever Premier League finish came in the 2004-05 season when Everton secured fourth place and there are some comparisons between that campaign to the one right now.

The build up to it saw star man Wayne Rooney sold to Manchester United, in some ways not dissimilar to Iliman Ndiaye joining Manchester City this time.

Last week, I asked Moyes how he reacts when he loses big-name players, and he referred back to this very same comparison.

"I thought to myself the world is going to end here if I don't keep Wayne, but we did really well without him," Moyes told me.

"We have to keep believing that if we are going to lose players we have to keep getting better."

Another similarity is the 2004-05 season saw the Toffees' tiny squad have 21 registered players. Some 22 years on, the number is the same.

This is the type of scenario where the manager comes into his own.

Since the deadline passed, Moyes has been inside the training ground, Finch Farm, creating a togetherness among players and staff.

He has been upbeat and made it clear that while he isn't happy with the end of the window, he does believe in the players that he has.

He will partly enjoy the siege mentality and feel that, while many have written Everton off already, this is a chance to go under the radar and achieve something special that no one else will expect.

After all, he has done it before and will use that experience to try to cause a shock more than two decades on from the club's best ever Premier League season.

articles.title: ‘We were like puppies’ – Pedri reveals how Lionel Messi welcomed him into the Barcelona locker room
articles.summary: Barcelona and Spain midfielder Pedri revealed his first interactions with Lionel Messi at the start of his career with Barca before Messi’s 2021 departure. M...
articles.body:
Barcelona and Spain midfielder Pedri revealed his first interactions with Lionel Messi at the start of his career with Barca before Messi's 2021 departure.

Many people forget that Pedri is not a graduate of Barcelona's iconic 'La Masia' academy, as the team signed a 17-year-old Pedri from Las Palmas for $5 million in 2020 before he earned his way into the senior squad.

Pedri's first full season with Barcelona was Lionel Messi's last, as the Catalan club couldn't afford to re-sign the legend, who left for PSG in 2021.

Pedri shares the full story of meeting Lionel Messi for the first time

In a letter on The Players Tribune , Pedri penned down his first interaction with Messi, describing how the legend helped him and new signing Rafael Trincao acclimatise to a locker room full of Spanish legends.

"When I opened the door to the players' area, guess who is the first person that I saw? It's Leo. He's standing in front of me. I was basically speechless. I tried to introduce myself. I don't know what I said. He just smiled and told me to relax and come into the dressing room."

"For the first few days, we used to just stay in the gym after training, because we were too embarrassed to go into the dressing room with all these legends: Busquets , Piqué , Jordi, Leo. We just stood around pretending that we were stretching forever."

"Finally, Leo walked by one day, and he must have figured out what was going on. He said: 'Hey, what are you guys doing in here? Come in and chill with us'. Leo brought us into the dressing room and showed us where to sit. We were like two puppies. 'Here? I can sit here?' I'll forever be grateful to him for that. Leo and Jordi broke the ice and made us so comfortable."

Even though they shared only one season as teammates, Pedri has repeatedly maintained that Messi is the player he views as the greatest of all time.

Pedri won the 2026 World Cup final against Messi's Argentina with Spain, and spoke on Messi's incredible ability and how his mind for the sport transcends everyone else.

"I had the luck of being able to play and train with him, and I enjoyed and learned a lot from him. Now, well, I enjoy him very much… He sees football a little before the others and knows where to be to score a goal. Of quality, he is overflowing; he has more than all the others. I think that what he does at his age, only he can do."

While Barcelona fans keep hoping they play together again if Messi somehow returns to end his career with the Catalan club, it's clear that Pedri would welcome that opportunity as well.

After coming up agonisingly short in last season's Champions League final, Arsenal begin what they hope will be a glorious European campaign at Napoli .

The Gunners were beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in May, with Gabriel missing the decisive kick after a 1-1 draw.

That was after Mikel Arteta's team topped the league phase with eight wins from eight and then went unbeaten during the knockout stages.

As for Napoli, their Champions League adventure was a big disappointment last term, as they finished in a lowly 30th place in the league phase.

New head coach Massimiliano Allegri, who replaced Antonio Conte this summer, will be confident of a better show from what is still a talented squad.

Napoli won their first Serie A game of the season, but go into this game after back-to-back losses.

Arsenal have only won on one of their last six away trips to face Italian sides in the Champions League (D1 L4), failing to score in five of those.

Hojlund scored 16 goals for the Partenopei last season on loan from Manchester United .

The forward's move to Napoli was made permanent for £38m after they secured Champions League qualification through Serie A last season.

The 23-year-old faced Arsenal five times as a United player, but he is yet to score or win against the Gunners.

Napoli will be without Scott McTominay as he required surgery due to an irregular heartbeat .

Last season the Scot featured in 44 games for the Italian club in all competitions, and scored 14 goals. Veteran midfielder Kevin de Bruyne has been used solely as an impact substitute this season.

He has come off the bench three times in Serie A, but has registered a goal and an assist in 85 minutes of play. De Bruyne has been involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal (eight goals, four assists), including five in his most recent three (three goals, two assists).

Harry Kane 's remarkable 2026 campaign is not only turning heads across Europe, it is making him the clear favorite for football's biggest individual prize.

According to the latest projections provided by Canada Spots Betting , the Bayern Munich striker has a 64% chance of winning the Ballon d'Or, putting him comfortably ahead of the competition.

Kane's consistency in front of goal, leadership, and influence for both club and country have made him the standout candidate. Whether it has been delivering in the Bundesliga, the Champions League, or on the international stage, the England captain has continued to prove why he is regarded as one of the world's elite players.

Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal sits in second place with an 18% probability, highlighting the teenager's incredible rise, while Manchester City midfielder Rodri follows with an 11% chance. Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé rounds out the leading contenders at 5%.

For Bayern Munich fans, it is another reminder of just how fortunate the club is to have a player of Kane's caliber leading the line. If these projections hold true, the Ballon d'Or could soon be heading to Munich (barring some kind of major screw job or journos acting irresponsibly).

How does the Ballon d'Or Supercomputer work? Well, check out the description for how it all came together:

The 2026 Ballon d'Or Supercomputer, conducted by CSB, is a probability model, not determined by human predictions or bias. This is based on a number of factors including their form during the 2025/26 season, other individual accolades they have won from the previous campaign, and the team trophies they have won in this time. The Supercomputer also factors in sentiment analysis of each player and their chances of winning the Ballon d'Or as well as betting market odds. The machine then simulates the Ballon d'Or rankings 10,000 times and constructs an average rankings table. Dashes in the table indicate a probability of absolutely zero per cent for that position while '<1%' indicates a less than one per cent chance of a player ranking in that spot. articles.title: Barcelona star Rodri personally calls Valencia squad over viral comments – report
articles.summary: Barcelona midfielder Rodri has reportedly taken the initiative to apologise to members of the Valencia squad after comments he made during the Catalan club’s...
articles.body:
Barcelona midfielder Rodri has reportedly taken the initiative to apologise to members of the Valencia squad after comments he made during the Catalan club's 5-0 victory went viral.

According to A Punt Radio , the summer signing personally contacted members of the Valencia team to explain what happened and apologise for his remarks.

The reported calls came after Movistar Plus cameras captured Rodri speaking to Pau Cubarsi while watching the remainder of the match.

Rodri did not appear to realise that his conversation was being picked up, leaving his comments open to public scrutiny after they circulated widely on social media.

During the match, Rodri was heard making a series of blunt observations about Valencia's players.

"They're really weak—these guys are really weak… Really weak. They're really bad, man. They're terrible.

"How did they finish last season? They didn't even make it past midfield in the second half…," Rodri told Cubarsi at different points while watching the remainder of the game.

The footage quickly became a talking point, with opinions divided over whether the Barcelona midfielder had gone too far or was simply speaking candidly to a teammate during what he believed was a private exchange.

Rodri's remarks after Valencia win made headlines. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Rather than allowing the controversy to linger, Rodri has chosen to address the situation on his own.

A Punt Radio reports that the midfielder called members of the Valencia squad himself because he wanted to apologise and clarify the circumstances surrounding his comments.

That move suggests Rodri recognised that words spoken privately can take on a different meaning once broadcast publicly, particularly when they concern opponents who have just suffered a heavy defeat.

For Valencia, the 5-0 scoreline was already difficult enough, and Rodri's remarks added further misery to an already uncomfortable evening.

articles.title: Konstantinos Karetsas substituted due to circulatory problems: ‘This is a concern for us’
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund’s Konstantinos Karetsas had to be substituted in the 27th minute of their UEFA Champions League victory over Villarreal due to circulatory...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund 's Konstantinos Karetsas had to be substituted in the 27th minute of their UEFA Champions League victory over Villarreal due to circulatory problems, the club have confirmed.

"Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems. Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests," BVB said on Tuesday evening.

Post Dortmund's 3-2 victory , sporting director Ole Book offered a further update. "We don't know more than that," he told Ruhr Nachrichten . "He was substituted due to circulatory problems. It happened very suddenly – he sat down and was taken to hospital for further examinations. We hope he recovers quickly and that it's nothing serious. This is a concern for us all right now."

Managing director Lars Ricken also sent his best wishes, and praised the team's response. "I have to compliment the team as well. It's not easy when a teammate is stretchered off and you don't exactly know what's wrong with him. You definitely feel that in a team but, we stood by each other."

articles.title: Where Estevao fits into Chelsea's all-star attack
articles.summary: A look at where Estevao Willian could feature for Chelsea this season after the reminder of his quality in his cameo against Arsenal.
articles.body:
A late flourish from Estevao Willian almost snatched Chelsea a draw at Arsenal on Sunday.

His curling strike was saved by goalkeeper David Raya to preserve Arsenal's lead, but it served as a reminder of the important role the 19-year-old Brazil winger could play in Xabi Alonso's side.

His game time has been limited so far this season by the club record £117m signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as the form of Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro .

The £51m signing from Brazilian club Palmeiras has played only 96 minutes this season, with 80 of those coming against League One side Luton Town in the Carabao Cup.

His remaining 16 minutes were in substitute appearances against Fulham and Premier League champions Arsenal, while he was unused as Chelsea held on for a narrow victory over Brighton in their third match of the campaign.

Reports in Brazil have suggested Estevao is unhappy with his lack of opportunities.

However, those claims have been denied by sources at Stamford Bridge and by people close to the player, some of whom have also expressed excitement about Chelsea's summer recruitment - including the arrival of Rogers.

Chelsea regard Estevao as one of a small group of untouchable players that includes Palmer, Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo .

The club have no intention of selling any of them, with Estevao central to the long-term planning of Alonso and Chelsea's leadership team.

There were also early discussions over a new contract, with Chelsea keen to reward key players with improved terms in the coming months, having done so for Joao Pedro.

Asked whether Estevao's lack of involvement meant he was unhappy, Alonso replied: "No, Este is ready, training well. The other day he had a great impact.

"He is fully involved with a very good attitude every day. I count on Este 100% because of his potential. He is so young but he is learning and adapting quickly. The season is long."

Estevao also suffered a serious grade-four hamstring tear late last season and missed the World Cup, so is expected to build his involvement through the campaign.

Estevao came on for Pedro Neto , who has been operating as a wing-back in Alonso's new system, as Chelsea chased an equaliser on Sunday.

It is difficult to imagine any other in-game circumstance in which Estevao would be asked to perform the same role, given the defensive and physical demands placed on players in that position.

Instead, Palmer occupies Estevao's preferred inside-right number 10 role.

Estevao and Palmer have shown encouraging signs when used together when Alonso has played a back four - but he has deployed that shape only against Luton Town in the Carabao Cup.

Displacing Palmer for league games could prove difficult as Alonso regards him as both a dressing-room leader and one of his key attacking threats.

Alonso has also fielded close to his strongest side even in the Carabao Cup, with Chelsea not involved in European competition and with the new head coach eager to establish his tactical principles as quickly as possible following his arrival.

Estevao is not alone in struggling for meaningful minutes early in the season and, should Leeds United win at Stamford Bridge in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, the Blues will have no further cup fixtures until the FA Cup in January.

That quietly makes Wednesday's game an important one in terms of keeping a 27-man squad satisfied.

Quenda , Emegha and Gittens are also hungry for more

Some of Chelsea's other young attackers have also struggled to start matches, with Palmer and Rogers beginning every game.

Joao Pedro has started all three league matches, while experienced striker Danny Welbeck led the line against Luton. That has limited Emmanuel Emegha , who joined from Strasbourg in the summer, to only one appearance on the bench.

Similarly, defender Aaron Anselmino is also yet to play and was only included in one squad, albeit both players are managing fitness issues.

Other attacking options, including Geovany Quenda and Jamie Gittens, have featured for only eight and 10 minutes respectively across Chelsea's four matches this season.

Quenda, who was signed despite interest from Manchester United in 2024, has also been left out of two of Alonso's matchday squads.

The situation might be even more challenging if it not for fitness issues affecting Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson , which have at times left Chelsea short in midfield.

Even then, summer signing Valentin Barco has been restricted to one start and a substitute appearance, as right-back Malo Gusto has started in midfield instead. Wing-back Marco Palestra also remains out injured.

If Chelsea had a fully fit squad available, they would have to leave six outfield players out of their matchday squad, with clubs permitted to name 11 starters and nine substitutes in English football.

Analysis of successful teams playing without European football suggests managers often rely on a relatively small core group of players.

Leicester City's surprise Premier League title-winning side of 2015-16 was achieved with only 14 players making more than 15 appearances in all competitions under Claudio Ranieri.

The following season, Chelsea won the title under Antonio Conte without European commitments. Only 13 players accumulated more than 1,500 minutes in all competitions.

While clubs are now allowed to make five substitutions, only 14 Newcastle United players exceeded the 1,500-minute mark when they qualified for the Champions League in 2022-23.

Perhaps the most relevant comparison is Manchester United after they finished third last season without European football. Only 13 players recorded more than 1,500 minutes across all competitions, although they exited both domestic cup competitions at an early stage.

For those on the fringes, including Estevao, a prolonged cup run could aide their chances of turning brief cameos into opportunities that Alonso cannot ignore.

articles.title: Thibaut Courtois reveals what Real Madrid must improve after Inter victory: ‘Match could have ended 4-4.’
articles.summary: Thibaut Courtois has admitted Real Madrid need to improve their control after surviving a chaotic Champions League encounter with Inter Milan.Real Madrid eve...
articles.body:
Thibaut Courtois has admitted Real Madrid need to improve their control after surviving a chaotic Champions League encounter with Inter Milan .

Real Madrid eventually secured a 2–1 victory , but the Belgian goalkeeper was forced to remain alert until the final whistle as Inter created enough opportunities to make the contest far more uncomfortable than the scoreline suggested.

Courtois believes the quality of both teams made the game particularly unpredictable, while acknowledging that Real Madrid failed to manage the match once they had taken the advantage.

"We played against a great opponent, one of the best teams in Europe. The match could have ended 4–4.

"We capitalised on their mistakes and should have sealed the win earlier; we didn't, and we were under pressure right until the end," he analysed.

The Real Madrid goalkeeper identified one particular weakness that allowed Inter to remain in contention.

Courtois' saves kept Real Madrid in the game against Inter. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Rather than simply pointing to defensive problems, Courtois highlighted the team's inability to slow the game down through possession.

"Sometimes we lack a bit of control, a bit of possession and a bit of composure.

"The match got far too frantic towards the end of the second half; that's something we need to improve on," he added.

Real Madrid's promising start under Mourinho

Despite the concerns, Courtois remains positive about Real Madrid's progress under Jose Mourinho.

The Champions League victory provided a response after their previous setback against Betis , although the goalkeeper believes that match should also have produced a better result.

Courtois was unbeatable against Inter Milan. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

"We're doing quite well. We should have beaten Betis, and today we were just a bit short. But we're playing well and we need to keep improving," he said.

Courtois also explained the thinking behind a crucial save from a powerful Hakan Calhanoglu free-kick, revealing that memories of previous goals influenced his decision-making.

" Rashford scored at my near post in El Clásico because I moved a little. It happened to me with Lamine Yamal at the World Cup.

"I knew he was going to aim for my near post because he remembered that goal, so I stayed still – that's why I don't move anymore.

"If he curls it over the wall and scores, you've got to give him credit," he concluded.

articles.title: Kovač explains decision to sub Arsenal loanee Nwaneri on and off against Villarreal
articles.summary: After coming on for Konstantinos Karetsas in the 27th minute of Borussia Dortmund's 3-2 Champions League win over Villarreal on Tuesday, Ethan Nwaneri was su...
articles.body:
After coming on for Konstantinos Karetsas in the 27th minute of Borussia Dortmund 's 3-2 Champions League win over Villarreal on Tuesday, Ethan Nwaneri was substituted again in the closing stages.

As BVB coach Niko Kovač explained after the game, the decision to take the Arsenal loanee off was related to his workload and the situation late in the game, with Dortmund defending a lead.

"He gave everything. If he had started the game, he probably would have come off around the 60th minute," Kovač said.

He added that the decision had "nothing" to do with the 19-year-old's performance.

"Quite the opposite, he was really good," Kovač underlined.

"It was great that he was able to have an impact on the team in such a short time."

Nwaneri wasn't directly involved in any of Dortmund's goals, but he took six shots after coming on and even hit the post with one of them.

articles.title: 'I cannot take my eyes off Bouaddi - he looks very special'
articles.summary: Ayyoub Bouaddi belied his age with a mature Champions League performance on his first Manchester City start to showcase why the club were so intent on signin...
articles.body:
Ayyoub Bouaddi belied his age with a mature Champions League performance on his first Manchester City start to showcase why the club were so intent on signing the 18-year-old.

And after two substitute appearances for City, he was handed his first start against Porto and did not look out of place during the 2-0 victory.

Erling Haaland will take the plaudits for his two goals, but it was Bouaddi who caught the eye with a tidy and assured performance in the middle of the park, signalling early signs that Rodri may not be too sorely missed after his departure.

"His age, his game – he looks absolutely born to do it," former Chelsea winger Pat Nevin said on BBC Radio 5 Live during the game.

"I cannot take my eyes off Bouaddi, he looks very special. The City fans had the fear of losing Rodri - I watched Bouaddi playing against Scotland at the World Cup, he has been very impressive so far."

Aged 18 years and 341 days, Bouaddi became the fourth-youngest player to start a Champions League match for City.

Question marks were raised around the size of the fee for a position on the pitch where players can be exposed, but Bouaddi seems to have settled in immediately and showcased why he will be a valuable option this season.

"He is very good," said manager Enzo Maresca. "Against Coventry , he lost two balls and after that he was inside our box and calm. Other players may have panicked but at 18, he is a fantastic player.

"Tonight, he was very good. He speaks French, English, Spanish perfect. He is different in how mature he is. This is why the club has made the effort for him to be with us."

Bouaddi completed 54 of his 55 passes, while he also topped the metrics across players of both sides for most dribbles (4), most times possession won (7) and contesting more duels (13).

"He did a really good game," said Haaland. "The last couple of weeks in training, he has been amazing. I think we have got a gem there, to be honest."

articles.title: Where do the Chargers stand in ESPN’s power index ahead of Week 1?
articles.summary: See where the Los Angeles Chargers stand in ESPN’s football power index ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Chargers ' 2026 season is only a few days away. Soon, they will kick off their 67th season in franchise history, and it is their biggest to date.

A lot of eyes will be on Los Angeles as they have all the tools to make a deep playoff run, something they haven't accomplished in nearly two decades. Nonetheless, all that will be forgotten if they live up to the hype this Fall.

ESPN's latest Football Power Index appears to be high on the Chargers. With the 2026 season kicking off soon, they ESPN's Matt Bowen and Seth Walder ranked the Bolts sixth.

According to the Power Index, entering Week 1, the Chargers have a 66.2% chance to make the playoffs and a 36.1% chance to win the AFC West.

On top of that, their projected wins are set at 9.8 and have the seventh-hardest strength of schedule.

The Chargers certainly don't have it easy entering the 2026 season. While their first two games are "easy" (on paper at least), it will be tough sledding in the middle of the season from Week 3 to 10.

That stretch is a gauntlet, featuring six teams that made the playoffs a season ago. The seventh team in that stretch didn't make the playoffs; that team was the Chiefs.

The Chargers have put themselves in a great position to make some noise this season. While a few question marks remain, particularly at interior offensive line, they believe they are better equipped this season to handle adversity or injuries.
